description.event: Orange juice flows continuously from the metal outlet inside the dispenser nozzle into a stationary transparent glass, impacts the rigid interior, and accumulates.
description.coupling: The dispenser is a prescribed inflow. The glass and tray use static effectors; liquid forces are not fed back into a rigid-body solve.

appearance.nozzle: The transparent outer shell remains visible with restrained optical influence; juice originates at the metal outlet inside it.
appearance.orange_juice_shader: Turbid pulp-style Principled surface with subsurface colour and wet coat.
appearance.environment: Warm café counter with plaster walls, fine limestone, framed wall art, and three real-scale orange props.
appearance.lighting: Broad neutral photographic softboxes with restrained warm ambience.
appearance.orange_props: Three grounded 7 cm citrus fruits with non-uniform silhouettes, peel pores, calyx, stems, and leaves.

simulation.solver: Blender 4.3.2 Mantaflow FLIP; prescribed inflow against static rigid effectors (no two-way coupling)
simulation.inlet: fixed 3.5 mm aperture (3.8503e-5 m^2 at resolution 160), outlet velocity (0, 0, -1.20) m/s; particles born from the integrated supply A*v*dt, level set corrected before pressure and meshing (appearance/flux_boundary.py)
simulation.paste_like_preset: edit_paste_like_viscosity: domain resolution 96, PIC (FLIP ratio 0), fractional inlet of the same area, implicit coupled strain-rate viscosity (physics/coupled_viscosity.py, CG 1e-7, SciPy 1.11.4 in assets/solver_vendor)
simulation.timed_stop: edit_stop_flow_at_2s stops the outlet at t = 2.0 s (Blender control frame 49); Mantaflow frame k is the state at k/24 s, so the edit applies from video frame 48
